statement: The monthly cost $M$, in dollars, for a climbing gym membership is given by $M(v) = 12v + 25$, where $v$ is the number of visits that month. Rosa visited the gym $4$ more times in May than in April. How many more dollars did she pay for May than for April?

choices.misconception: I worked out $M(4) = 12(4) + 25 = 73$, which is the cost of a month with 4 visits, not the extra cost of 4 more visits.
I mixed up the two numbers and charged the 25 dollars for each extra visit, so I got $4 \times 25 = 100$.
I added the 12 and the 25 and treated $37$ dollars as the cost of each extra visit, so I got $4 \times 37 = 148$.

hints: Which part of $12v + 25$ changes when $v$ changes?
The 25 dollars is paid every month no matter how many visits. Only the $12v$ part grows.
Each extra visit adds $12$ dollars, so $4$ extra visits add $4 \times 12$ dollars.

solutions.reliable: The fee of $25$ dollars is the same every month, so it cancels: $M(v + 4) - M(v) = 12(v + 4) + 25 - (12v + 25) = 48$. May cost $48$ dollars more than April, whatever the April number of visits was.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
